Construct landmark risk sets

Source: R/landmark_data.R
landmark_data.Rd

landmark_data() builds the outcome side of a landmark analysis. For each landmark time \(s\) it keeps every subject who is still under observation and event-free at \(s\). It moves the time origin to \(s\) and, optionally, administratively censors follow-up at a fixed post-landmark horizon. The result stacks all landmarks into one long table with one row per eligible subject-landmark pair.

Longitudinal covariates are not handled here. Attach them afterwards with add_landmark_covariates().

Usage

landmark_data(data, id, time, status, landmarks, horizon = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per subject, holding follow-up time, event status and any baseline predictors.

id

<tidy-select> The subject identifier column. It must be unique and non-missing. Its type is preserved in .id.

time

<tidy-select> Numeric, non-negative, finite time from the common origin (time zero) to the first event or censoring.

status

<tidy-select> Event indicator. It is either:

  • numeric: 0 for censoring and positive integers 1, 2, ... for event types. Codes other than the target cause are treated as competing events by fit_landmark().

  • factor: the first level is censoring and later levels are event types. They are recoded to 0, 1, 2, ... in level order. The mapping is stored in the object's configuration.

landmarks

A non-empty numeric vector of unique, non-negative landmark times on the original time scale. Landmarks are processed in ascending order regardless of input order.

horizon

NULL (default) for follow-up to each subject's observed time, or a single positive number giving the follow-up window relative to each landmark. For example, horizon = 180 at landmark 90 ends follow-up at original time 270.

Value

A landmark_tbl, which is a tibble subclass. Its leading columns are:

  • .id: subject identifier, with the original type.

  • .landmark: landmark time on the original scale.

  • .time: follow-up since the landmark. It is always strictly positive.

  • .status: integer, 0 for censored or 1, 2, ... for the event type.

  • .horizon: the configured horizon, or NA when follow-up is unbounded.

The remaining baseline columns follow. Rows are ordered by landmark, then by the original row order of data. Use tibble::as_tibble() to drop the class and metadata.

Details

Eligibility. A subject is in the risk set at landmark \(s\) exactly when \(T_i > s\). A subject whose event or censoring is recorded at \(s\) is not eligible.

Time and status. For eligible subjects, .time is \(T_i - s\) when horizon is NULL, and \(\min(T_i - s, w)\) otherwise. .status keeps the original code when \(T_i - s \le w\), so an event exactly at the horizon is retained. Otherwise .status becomes 0.

Columns. The original id, time and status columns are replaced by the reserved columns below. All other columns are carried over unchanged, and subjects are never dropped for missing baseline predictors. If data already contains a reserved column name, the function throws an error.

A landmark with no eligible subjects triggers a warning. It contributes zero rows but still appears in the configuration and in the printed counts.

Examples

subjects <- data.frame(
  patient_id    = 1:10,
  followup_days = c(20, 30, 48, 65, 85, 110, 145, 190, 250, 270),
  event         = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 1),
  age           = c(12, 15, 11, 17, 9, 14, 13, 16, 10, 15)
)

lm_dat <- landmark_data(
  subjects,
  id = patient_id,
  time = followup_days,
  status = event,
  landmarks = c(30, 60, 90),
  horizon = 180
)
lm_dat
#> <landmark_tbl> 3 landmark(s): 30, 60, 90
#> Horizon: 180 (relative to each landmark)
#> Subjects: 8 at risk in current rows (10 in source data)
#> Source columns: id = patient_id, time = followup_days, status = event
#>  landmark n_at_risk n_censored n_event_1 n_event_2
#>        30         8          3         3         2
#>        60         7          3         2         2
#>        90         5          1         3         1
#> 
#> # A tibble: 20 × 6
#>      .id .landmark .time .status .horizon   age
#>    <int>     <dbl> <dbl>   <int>    <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1     3        30    18       1      180    11
#>  2     4        30    35       2      180    17
#>  3     5        30    55       0      180     9
#>  4     6        30    80       1      180    14
#>  5     7        30   115       2      180    13
#>  6     8        30   160       1      180    16
#>  7     9        30   180       0      180    10
#>  8    10        30   180       0      180    15
#>  9     4        60     5       2      180    17
#> 10     5        60    25       0      180     9
#> 11     6        60    50       1      180    14
#> 12     7        60    85       2      180    13
#> 13     8        60   130       1      180    16
#> 14     9        60   180       0      180    10
#> 15    10        60   180       0      180    15
#> 16     6        90    20       1      180    14
#> 17     7        90    55       2      180    13
#> 18     8        90   100       1      180    16
#> 19     9        90   160       0      180    10
#> 20    10        90   180       1      180    15

# Without a horizon, follow-up runs to each subject's observed time
landmark_data(subjects, patient_id, followup_days, event, landmarks = 60)
#> <landmark_tbl> 1 landmark(s): 60
#> Horizon: none (follow-up to observed time)
#> Subjects: 7 at risk in current rows (10 in source data)
#> Source columns: id = patient_id, time = followup_days, status = event

#>
